title: Arduino-Based CPR Trainer with Live Telemetry
content: Current resuscitation-education guidelines recommend feedback devices during CPR training. This paper describes a low-cost trainer built from an Arduino Uno, an HC-SR04 ultrasonic ranging module, a 16×2 character display, two LEDs, and an active buzzer. The sensor sits at the bottom of a shaft in a compressible foam block and reports the distance to a reflector plate above it in whole centimeters. The firmware takes the deepest point of each compression, counts the compression when the distance returns past a start threshold, and classifies it as too shallow, acceptable, or too deep. A 110 per minute metronome cues the rate, and a cycle of 30 compressions is followed by a 5 s pause for rescue breaths. Readings are streamed over USB to a Python server that pushes them to a live web graph. Firmware analysis shows that integer truncation makes the "acceptable" band about 2 cm wide, spanning roughly 4–6 cm or 5–7 cm of depth depending on the true rest distance, against the 5–6 cm guideline. It also identifies counting and timing hazards. The device has not yet been evaluated quantitatively; a measurement protocol is proposed. This is a training aid; no clinical claims are made.
